scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You never gave them your number, yet they call about loans and offers every day. How did they get it?

scenes.name: leaks
scenes.text: Numbers leak through data breaches, shared forms, shopping sign ups, and apps that read your contacts.

scenes.name: lists
scenes.text: These get bundled into lists and sold, often tagged with your city, age, or interests.

scenes.name: dialer
scenes.text: Software dials huge numbers of calls at once. Some even try numbers in sequence.

scenes.name: answer
scenes.text: If you pick up, your number gets marked as active, and becomes more valuable. So you get even more calls.

scenes.name: callerid
scenes.text: Apps like Truecaller name callers using crowdsourced contact data, and spam reports from millions of users.

scenes.name: fight
scenes.text: In India, turn on DND through TRAI, report spam, and remember, registered telemarketers must use numbers starting with one four zero.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Leak, list, dial, flag. Now you know. Follow for more on how things really work.
